ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The main transition-state structure in the figure contains a central S; S is connected to R1, an O, and the carbon on the right; this O is also connected to the acyl carbon above, and the acyl carbon is double-bonded to O and connected to an alkyl line segment. The carbon on the right is connected to R2, and a C-H bond is drawn. An AcO− component is also shown separately below the image; the curved arrows in the figure are ignored according to the problem statement. Reasoning: Count only bonds between non-hydrogen atoms. The heavy-atom bonds in the main transition-state structure are S-R1, S-O, O-C(acyl), C=O, acyl C-alkyl carbon, S-C, and C-R2, for a total of 7; the drawn C-H bond is excluded. The other AcO− component is expanded as acetate CH3-C(=O)-O−, with heavy-atom bonds C-C, C=O, and C-O, for a total of 3. The total is 7 + 3 = 10.

method.method_draft: First list the heavy-atom bonds in the main transition-state structure shown: S-R1, S-O, O-C(acyl), C=O, acyl C-CH3/alkyl line, S-C, and C-R2 = 7 bonds. Exclude the drawn C-H bond because the prompt says to exclude bonds involving hydrogen. Then include the separate AcO− component: expand AcO− as CH3-C(=O)-O−, giving C-C, C=O, and C-O = 3 more heavy-atom bonds. Add 7 + 3 to obtain 10.
